text:
Jon H.: forwarding a phishing report submitted via security form. Subject: "Invoice Overdue — Action Required". Sender: invoices@payable-payments.com (domain looks like payable-payments[.]com)
Maya P.: got it at 09:22. link asked me to sign in to view invoice. I did NOT enter creds and reported via the form.
Jon H.: full headers & message dump below. pasting the body snippet.
Jon H.: ```
From: invoices@payable-payments.com
To: maya@redwood.com
Subject: Invoice Overdue - Action Required
Body: Please sign in to view your invoice: https://payable-payments.com/secure/login?invoice=3421
Attachment: invoice_3421.html
```
Aisha K.: thanks. @OpsOnCall can you sandbox the link and attachment? suspect credential harvest. :eyes:
OpsOnCall: running sandbox now (phish-sandbox). kicking off analysis.
PhishSandboxBot: Sandbox report for url https://payable-payments.com/secure/login?invoice=3421
PhishSandboxBot: Verdict: MALICIOUS
PhishSandboxBot: Indicators: credential-harvest-form, TLS cert mismatch (CN != payable-payments.com), host geolocated CN, form POSTs to https://auth-payable.com/collect
PhishSandboxBot: Screenshots and HAR saved to: https://sandbox.internal/artefacts/1714501234
Ravi S.: confirmed via proxy logs. I see a single client IP (10.8.33.72) with a GET then a POST to auth-payable.com from Maya's workstation. Query used: 
Ravi S.: ```kibana
index=proxy-logs | where client_ip=="10.8.33.72" and url contains "auth-payable" | sort @timestamp desc
```
Ravi S.: looks like no successful credential exchange (no 200 from collect endpoint after form submit) and no SSO token exchanges observed. MFA logs show no bypass.
Aisha K.: containment plan: 1) block sender and domain in email gateway; 2) add IOCs to detection lists (payable-payments.com, auth-payable.com); 3) revoke SSO sessions for Maya and force re-auth; 4) search for other clicks and notify users who clicked; 5) add sample to phishing training repo.
Jon H.: blocked sender & domain in gateway (rule EG-4521). quarantined matching inbound messages. :lock:
OpsOnCall: added domain to quarantine list and updated inbound parser. initiating retro-hunt for similar messages.
Ravi S.: revoked Maya's SSO sessions (Okta) and flagged account for elevated monitoring. Created ticket SEC-2026-118 to track. So far only Maya's client shows POSTs.
Maya P.: thanks, I confirmed I didn't type anything. appreciate the quick help.
Aisha K.: good. Jon can you draft a calm company-wide awareness note that includes the indicators, how to report, and what to do if you clicked? avoid naming the user.
Jon H.: drafting now. will post here for approval.
Ravi S.: post-incident actions: 1) push detection rule to prod for hostnames matching pattern (dash + payable) + outbound form POSTs to non-org auth domains; 2) add sample to phish repo and training; 3) update runbook with this IOC pattern. I can own detection (48h ETA).
Aisha K.: assign owners: @Ravi S. detection, @Jon H. comms.
Jon H.: draft comms: ```
Subject: Phishing attempt reported to security — please review
We received a phishing email impersonating an invoice provider. If you clicked the link but did not enter credentials, you do not need to change passwords but please report immediately. Indicators: sender invoices@payable-payments.com, links to payable-payments.com and auth-payable.com. If you entered credentials, contact IT immediately and rotate credentials + enable MFA.
```
Maya P.: maybe add a quick tip: check TLS certs and hover on links before clicking.
Aisha K.: noted. once detection rule is live and comms sent we'll close. add to retrospective: consider blocking top 500 suspicious registrars and adding dashed-hostname heuristics. :thumbsup:
PhishSandboxBot: Artifact saved to SEC_BOX/2026/1714501234
Jon H.: comms sent at 11:12, copied secops.
Aisha K.: closing thread after detection pushed and training updated. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
